# Model Mountain — hackathon completion checklist

Source: https://sparthill-ibm-2026.devpost.com/ and /rules, read 2026-10-23.
The page lists October 24, 2026, 10:00 a.m. PDT. Organizer announcements override.

| Requirement | Model Mountain deliverable | Completion evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Clear responsible-AI problem and affected users | Explain business assistants exposed to poisoned documents and unauthorized actions | Overview and submission narrative |
| Working AI prototype | Authenticated control plane and compatible remote model/MIA execution | API tests plus genuine worker artifacts |
| Responsible AI and measurable impact | Source/tenant boundaries, inert actions, privacy, abstention and independent evaluation | Negative tests, failure cases and measured limits |
| Technical execution and feasibility | Vercel CPU web/API; separate Kaggle GPU jobs | Reproducible setup, deployment, compatibility matrix |
| Innovation | Compare external controls with model-internal interventions | Actual capture/intervention evidence, not classifier-only claims |
| Demo | Accessible live app or short video (three minutes or less preferred) | Verify judge access and prepare demonstration script |
| Technical review | Repository and README with setup instructions | Repository URL and documented versions |
| Honest attribution | Pre-existing baseline, models, IBM libraries, data and AI assistance | DISCLOSURE.md; credit licenses |

Team submission needs title, team/member names, summary, detailed description, technology
list, limitations and next steps. One project per team; maximum five students. Team
eligibility and registration are handled by the human team. Do not assert IBM Bob use:
it is encouraged in the event rules, not established as used here.

Release acceptance is tracked through the Model Mountain hub, project ID
16f864bfa1303fc9, at http://127.0.0.1:8776. This checklist describes required evidence;
it does not claim pending deployment or GPU experiments are complete.
